summary: GRAVEYARD falsification revision covered all 12 b03 companies using cumulative Beta evidence plus the newer same-cycle Alpha primary acquisitions. AUR and SMR no longer lack the capitalization denominator that previously blocked this lane; their financing risk is now quantifiable enough for Chief treatment. SERV remains the only red-team company blocker because its current concentration and post-financing runway are still stale. Mature-name backlog/cycle risks remain risk factors, not manufactured promotion blockers.

materialFindings.finding: Record AI-test demand remains vulnerable to geography/customer concentration; FY2025 Taiwan/China/Korea revenue evidence reinforces the semiconductor-cycle falsifier.
Cyclical automation recovery and normalization complexity remain valid falsifiers; Alpha still lacks the current issuer-primary dossier, but this does not create a distinct red-team evidence gate.
Program wins and SuperVision growth coexist with ASP/mix pressure and higher-hardware gross-margin risk; commercialization success need not imply margin expansion.

Historical Uber concentration of 71% of 2023 revenue plus only stale runway evidence makes current concentration/financing dependence unreproducible; this is a present lane-relevant blocker, not generic future uncertainty.

June 2026 cash plus short-term investments of $1.217B against six-month $493M net loss and shares rising to 1.998B from 1.943B provides enough primary denominator to carry dilution/runway risk explicitly. Economic proof remains weak but no longer requires blocking this lane.
Data-center/electrification acceleration can normalize and acquisition contribution can flatter growth; diversified end markets reduce single-theme fragility.
Backlog remains vulnerable to project timing, labor, fixed-price execution and mix; current underwriting dossier gap belongs to Alpha rather than a separate red-team blocker.
Large data-center/LNG awards increase concentration and lumpiness; primary backlog growth confirms demand but not riskless conversion.
Nuclear/data-center duration is offset by integration, regulatory and capital-intensity risks; current financial dossier gap is an underwriting blocker, not a reason to invent bearish evidence.
PPAs and generation assets retain hedge/basis/counterparty and integration sensitivities; current financial dossier gap is underwriting-specific.
Backlog quality remains heterogeneous across product/service/tax assumptions; current issuer financial/concentration refresh remains underwriting-specific.

FY2025 primary evidence quantifies $31.5M revenue, $664M net loss, $459.6M operating cash use and $1.300B net common-stock issuance proceeds. This closes the missing dilution denominator for red-team treatment while preserving nonbinding-project risk and extreme financing dependence.

gatingGaps: current customer concentration and post-financing runway required for reproducible dilution/survival treatment

contradictions: AUR has substantial runway but still minimal revenue and continuing dilution.
SMR has substantial liquidity but it is materially equity-financed while flagship deployment remains nonbinding.
unknowns: No canonical live crowding/short-interest feed was required or fabricated; absence does not block baseline treatment.
peerRequests: Company-underwriting/source-integrity: close SERV current concentration and post-financing runway; Chief should preserve AUR/SMR financing risk as explicit risk rather than a binary blocker now that primary denominators exist.
